source_refs.note: Topic 1.8.2, printed page 15, as printed: the reactions with oxygen and the magnesium-flare photo caption.

blocks.text: Sodium burns in oxygen with a golden yellow flame to produce a white solid mixture of sodium oxide and sodium peroxide. Sodium is kept under kerosene oil to prevent its reaction with air. It reacts vigorously with oxygen in open air to form peroxide.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: This equation is not balanced: 2 Na atoms on the left, 4 on the right. The balanced equation is 2Na(s) + O₂(g) → Na₂O₂(s).
Under special conditions like limited O₂ or high temperature, sodium oxide is formed.
Magnesium burns in oxygen with an intense white flame to give white solid magnesium oxide.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Magnesium oxide is the white solid named in the sentence above, so it is 2MgO(s), not (g): 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s).
Magnesium powder burns very rapidly with an intense white flame. This has led to its use in fireworks and S.O.S. flares
